messages.subject: all pvalues from scanone
parts:
I am trying to get a pvalue for every SNP and for every every phenotype from scanone. When I use summary() to incorporate the LOD scores of scanone and, separately, the pvalues from scanone w/permutations, the output with format = "allpheno" is the highest LOD (or lowest pvalue) for each phenotype for each chromosome. The maximum number of results for each phenotype is 20 (19 autosomal chromosomes + X in this case). My problem is that I want to see all of the relevant LODs and pvalues on each chromosome, not just the best result per chromosome. What is the proper way to incorporate the permutations and the format = "allpheno" ?   Thank you. 

#pseudocode that is giving top result per chromosome 
#calculate QTL
out.i <- scanone(sug, pheno.col = i, method="hk")

# run permutations
operm <- scanone(sug, pheno.col = i, method="hk", n.perm=1000, perm.Xsp=TRUE) 

#values stored in output
x=summary(out.i, perms=operm, format = "allpheno", pvalues=TRUE) 
y=cbind(phenonames[i], x[])

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] all pvalues from scanone
parts:
format="allpheno" is only used if there are multiple phenotypes in the results, so in the code that you show, you should get a warning in summary() that says

With just one LOD column, format="onepheno" used.

R/qtl doesn't have an option to get p-values at all positions, but if you feed one row at a time to summary, you can get them.

pval <- sapply(1:nrow(out), function(i) summary(out[i,], perms=operm, pvalues=TRUE)$pval)

To add them to the output, you could use:

out_rev <- cbind(pheno=phenonames[i], as.data.frame(out), pval=pval)

karl
